findings.title: Enemy-reset acceptance criterion on persistent closure does not explicitly restate status-effect/displacement clearing
findings.description: GDD 'Loss' explicitly requires that 'no target, last-known-position, search, attack, status-effect, or displacement state carries over from the failed run.' The floor-run-restart-persistent-closure work item lists enemy-status-effect-displacement as a dependency and its generic acceptance criterion ('invoke reset entry points for every implemented persistent owner beyond the bootstrap set') covers it structurally, but the item's specific enemy-reset acceptance criterion only names 'no retained target or search state' and omits status-effect/displacement explicitly. This is not currently exploitable as a gap because the dependency edge and generic full-closure gate both require enemy-status-effect-displacement's own reset entry point to be invoked, so an implementer cannot skip it without violating the generic criterion. This is a clarity improvement, not a missing obligation.

gdd_evidence.reference: GDD §2 Win and Loss Conditions — Loss
gdd_evidence.requirement: no target, last-known-position, search, attack, status-effect, or displacement state carries over from the failed run

findings.recommended_change: Optionally expand the enemy-reset acceptance criterion on floor-run-restart-persistent-closure to explicitly name status-effect and displacement clearing alongside target/search state, for readability during future decomposition; not required for correctness given the existing dependency edge and generic closure gate.

notes: Scope for this pass was restricted to: zero-health loss, Floor Run/Restart orchestration, staged/current-owner and full persistent closure, win/loss, final escape/victory, input shutdown, and You Escaped presentation, per the PARALLEL AUDIT SCOPE override.

Verified against repository state that PlayerHealth.cs, PlayerMana.cs, PlayerMovement.cs, and DoorInteractable.cs currently expose no restore/reset/zero-health-event/suspend interfaces, and that no Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave, enemy, restart-orchestrator, or victory/escape code exists anywhere under Assets/. This matches every repository_state/repository_evidence claim made by the candidate's floor-run-restart-bootstrap, floor-run-restart-persistent-closure, player-health, and final-escape-victory nodes.

All depends_on edges inspected within this territory (floor-run-restart-bootstrap, floor-run-restart-persistent-closure, final-escape-victory) target kind=implementation nodes only; no feature-to-feature dependency edges were found in this territory.

GDD reference labels cited by the candidate in this territory (e.g. 'Floor-run restart ownership', 'Victory/input-shutdown ownership', 'Player Health ownership') correspond to real bolded GDD subheadings/labels in Docs/GDD/No_Safe_Circle_GDD.md; no fabricated 'VERIFIED CLOSURE' or verifier-provenance labels were used as GDD evidence in this territory.

The candidate's decision to represent the loss trigger under floor-run-restart rather than duplicating it under win-loss-conditions/final-escape-victory is a reasonable and explicitly justified split (win-side vs loss-side ownership), consistent with the GDD's own architectural split between Game Flow/Victory and the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator.

final-escape-victory's suspend-interface dependency set (player-movement, door-open-interaction, fireball, frost-field, force-wave) matches the GDD's explicit five-owner list ('Player Movement, Door/Interaction, Fireball, Frost Field, and Force Wave') exactly; enemy systems are correctly excluded since the GDD does not list them as suspend-interface owners.

requirements.reference: GDD §2 Win and Loss Conditions — Loss
requirements.requirement: Reaching zero health restarts the entire floor by design; this is an intentional single-attempt structure, not a placeholder.
requirements.explanation: The loss->restart trigger is organized as its own feature (floor-run-restart) which decomposes into the bootstrap and persistent-closure implementation nodes; this is a legitimate work-item representation of a distinct required mechanic.

requirements.reference: GDD §2 Win and Loss Conditions — Loss
requirements.requirement: Restart resets all run-persistent gameplay state to the floor's initial state, including Player Health, Player Mana/regen-delay, player position/movement, Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave, persistent enemy objects/health, pursuit/search/status/attack state, Active Enemy Registry bookkeeping, door lifecycle/crossing/durability state, and encounter activation/admission state.
requirements.explanation: Every named participant appears either in the bootstrap's currently-existing-owner set or as an explicit dependency of floor-run-restart-persistent-closure, whose acceptance criteria require full participation before closure is considered complete.

requirements.requirement: Player Health's observable zero-health/death transition triggers the shared Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator, which invokes owned reset entry points rather than reaching into or duplicating another system's internal state.
requirements.explanation: floor-run-restart-bootstrap's acceptance criteria explicitly require subscribing to an owner-exposed zero-health/death transition and calling only exposed reset entry points, matching this GDD contract directly.

requirements.requirement: Early implementation may validate the orchestrator against only currently-existing persistent systems, but full restart closure remains required work until every implemented state owner participates.
requirements.explanation: The staged bootstrap/closure split and the closure item's explicit 'not considered complete while any implemented owner does not participate' criterion preserve this two-stage GDD-authorized structure without treating the bootstrap as terminal.

requirements.reference: GDD §2 Win and Loss Conditions — Loss / Floor-run restart ownership
requirements.requirement: Each persistent enemy is returned to its original authored encounter/spawn region and initial AI state on restart; no target, last-known-position, search, attack, status-effect, or displacement state carries over from the failed run.
requirements.explanation: Persistent-closure's acceptance criteria plus its dependencies on enemy-pursuit-search-foundation and enemy-status-effect-displacement (each required to expose its own reset entry point) durably cover this; see F1 for a minor clarity suggestion, not a coverage gap.

requirements.requirement: Each spell owner (Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave) exposes a reset entry point for any owned state that can still be active when a floor restart occurs.
requirements.explanation: All three spells are named dependencies of floor-run-restart-persistent-closure with reasons explicitly citing their owned reset-state obligations, matching the GDD's per-spell reset ownership split.

requirements.requirement: The shared Player Health system exposes owner-controlled damage/restore interfaces plus an observable zero-health/death transition consumed by the Floor Run/Restart Orchestrator; restoration is clamped to maximum health and other systems never write player-health state directly.
requirements.explanation: player-health's acceptance criteria require exactly these interfaces (clamped restore, observable zero-health/death event, orchestrator-consumed reset entry point), matching repository evidence that none currently exist on PlayerHealth.cs.

requirements.reference: GDD §2 Win and Loss Conditions — Win
requirements.requirement: Victory occurs when the shared doorway-crossing state confirms the wizard crossed to the forward side of the final door; the win condition does not implement a separate crossing detector.
requirements.explanation: final-escape-victory's acceptance criteria and its dependency on doorway-crossing-state directly capture this single-source-of-truth crossing trigger.

requirements.reference: GDD §2 Win and Loss Conditions — Win
requirements.requirement: Once victory is confirmed, normal gameplay input (movement, door interaction, Fireball, Frost Field, Force Wave) stops and a simple 'You Escaped' overlay is displayed; no additional post-victory progression, menu flow, or meta-progression is required.
requirements.explanation: final-escape-victory's acceptance criteria explicitly require the overlay and explicitly note no further progression/menu flow is implemented, matching the GDD's explicit scope-closing statement.

requirements.requirement: A reusable Game Flow/Victory capability owns the won-state transition, overlay display, and gameplay-shutdown coordination; Player Movement, Door/Interaction, Fireball, Frost Field, and Force Wave each expose an owner-controlled suspend/re-enable interface that stops already-active input-driven activity (not merely blocks new commands) and is consumed rather than having internals mutated directly.
requirements.explanation: final-escape-victory's acceptance criteria and its five owner-interface dependencies (player-movement, door-open-interaction, fireball, frost-field, force-wave) match this ownership/suspend contract exactly, including the 'stop already-active activity, not just block new input' nuance.

requirements.reference: GDD §4 Development Agent Ownership Invariants — Final escape/victory coordination
requirements.requirement: Final escape/victory coordination owns only the won-state transition, gameplay-suspension coordination, and victory presentation; it must not reach into movement, door, or spell internals to stop them.
requirements.explanation: This is the process-invariant half of a compound passage whose runtime behavior half is separately captured as acceptance criteria on final-escape-victory (R10); the invariant itself is durably represented as a typed pipeline_constraint non-code record.

requirements.reference: GDD §4 Shared Context and Coordination Rules — Current prototype scene-builder lock
requirements.requirement: Under the current scene-built UI approach, final-victory work that creates/configures the 'You Escaped' overlay must take exclusive-write locks on DoorPrototypeSceneBuilder.cs and DoorPrototype.unity.
requirements.explanation: final-escape-victory's exclusive_resources list cites exactly this builder/scene lock with the matching GDD rationale, and the durable typed pipeline_constraint record exists in non_code_requirements.

requirements.requirement: Adding later rooms or stateful systems must extend the reset participants without redesigning the orchestration contract.
requirements.explanation: The closure item's acceptance criteria describe extending the same orchestrator to invoke additional owners as they become implemented, preserving the contract rather than redesigning it, matching this forward-compatibility requirement.
